verdict_reason: The three per-matrix quantities are the standard definitions and are computed correctly. On a planted diagonal spectrum sigma = 64,63,...,1 the closed forms ||W||_F = 299.06521028, sigma_max = 64, stable rank = sum(sigma^2)/sigma_max^2 = 21.83593750 are returned at rel 1.9e-8 / 0.0 / 3.9e-8; on all 48 gpt2 transformer weight matrices the values match LIVE weightwatcher 0.7.7 at mean rel 1.5e-4 and max rel 3.0e-4 (float32 SVD noise). The min(raw_srank, min(m,n)) clip is a mathematical no-op (stable rank <= rank always) that only fires on numerical error.
comparable_reason: Two independent failures, both measured. (1) Scale: mean_stable_rank has Spearman +0.683 with d_model and +0.683 with log(params) over 61 models. (2) Parameterization: for y = W2 W1 x with (W1,W2) = (I_4, I_4) vs (100*I_4, 0.01*I_4) -- bit-identical functions -- mean_frobenius_norm goes 2.00000 -> 100.01000, mean_spectral_norm 1.00000 -> 50.00500 and norm_uniformity 1.000000 -> 0.000200. Stable rank IS invariant to that reparameterization (4.0 both times), so it survives (1) only. Layout matters too: the same identity map as one 4x4 parameter reports Frobenius 2.0 / stable rank 4.0, but as two concatenated 2x4 blocks reports 1.41421 / 2.0 -- 29.3% and 50.0% shifts from a fusion choice, which is exactly what differs between fused-QKV and split-QKV architectures in the zoo.
normalized_variant: mean_stable_rank_scalenorm (= mean_stable_rank / d_model; NORMALIZERS in src/blme/normalization.py), plus the in-task code twins mean_stable_rank_normalized (= stable_rank / min(m,n)) and mean_rms_weight_scale (= ||W||_F / sqrt(mn))
normalized_ok_detail: Nothing dimensionless is emitted. stable_rank/min(m,n) and RMS weight scale ||W||_F/sqrt(mn) would be the natural named companions; neither exists. norm_uniformity = max(0, 1-CV) is a shape statistic across layers, not a width normalisation, and it is itself reparameterization-sensitive (1.0 -> 0.0002 above).
github_reason: The definitional source (Rudelson & Vershynin 2007, JACM) is a theory paper and released no code -- I searched and none exists. The cross-check reference the task itself names, WeightWatcher, WAS installed (0.7.7) and RUN live on gpt2 fp32. Name-aligned over 48 modules: stable_rank mean rel 1.5e-4 / max 3.0e-4; WW's 'norm' field == ||W||_F^2 to max rel 3.0e-4; WW's 'sv_max' == BLME's spectral norm to max rel 1.0e-4. Note for readers: WW reports norm and spectral_norm SQUARED, BLME reports them unsquared -- the definitions agree, the conventions differ.
paper_reason: Rudelson & Vershynin publish the definition r = ||A||_F^2/||A||_2^2 but no transformer-weight value. The nearest published targets are Martin, Peng & Mahoney 2021 Table 2 for GPT2-small: <log||W||_F> = 2.04 and <log||W||_inf> = 2.54 over 49 layers. Per-matrix over gpt2's 48 modules BLME gives mean log10||W||_F = 2.1892 (+7.3%) and mean log10(lambda_max) = 2.827 (+11.3%); live WeightWatcher 0.7.7 gives the IDENTICAL 2.1892 and 2.827, so the residual gap is WW 0.2.7 -> 0.7.7 version drift, not a BLME error. The task's own aggregation (mean of values within a block, then across blocks) is not the paper's (mean of log10 per matrix), so mean_frobenius_norm / mean_spectral_norm are not like-for-like targets for those table entries.
confounds_reason: Over 61 models: mean_stable_rank Spearman +0.683 with d_model, +0.525 with n_layers, +0.683 with log(params). mean_spectral_norm -0.651 with log(vocab) and mean_frobenius_norm -0.404 with log(vocab). norm_uniformity is the one clean column (-0.073 / -0.131 / -0.053). Stable rank is bounded above by min(m,n), which is a deterministic function of d_model, so this association is partly structural.
defects: SVD failure and non-finite weights fail OPEN. Verified: an all-NaN weight returns frob = nan, spectral = nan, stable_rank = nan, and np.nanmean then drops it silently, so a block containing one clean I_4 and one corrupt matrix reports exactly the clean-only numbers (2.0 / 1.0 / 4.0). No attempted/succeeded counts and no warning field are emitted, so a partially-failed model is indistinguishable from a fully-successful one downstream.

The reported quantities are not invariant under function-preserving reparameterization: (I,I) vs (100I, 0.01I) computes the same function but moves mean_frobenius_norm 50x, mean_spectral_norm 50x and norm_uniformity from 1.0 to 0.0002. Any model family that differs in where it puts scale (LayerNorm gain vs projection weight) is measured on the parameterization, not the model.

Aggregation is over exposed parameter tensors, so fused vs split projections change the value: the same linear map as one 4x4 gives Frobenius 2.0 / stable rank 4.0, as two 2x4 blocks gives 1.41421 / 2.0 (-29.3% / -50.0%). GPT-2's fused c_attn and Llama's separate q/k/v_proj are exactly this difference.
mean_stable_rank is emitted raw and is dimension-bounded (Spearman +0.683 with d_model); no stable_rank/min(m,n) companion exists.
norm_uniformity's floor at max(0, 1-CV) censors every model with CV > 1 to the same value 0.0, discarding the ordering among the least uniform models.
fix: Fail closed: emit n_matrices_attempted / n_matrices_succeeded (and a warning list) rather than letting nanmean hide failures. Add explicitly named dimensionless companions -- stable_rank_normalized = stable_rank/min(m,n) and rms_weight_scale = ||W||_F/sqrt(mn) -- and keep the raw norms as architecture-conditioned diagnostics. Canonicalize fused vs split projections by module role before averaging so QKV layout is not measured as geometry. Report CV itself alongside norm_uniformity so the clamp is not lossy. No change is needed to the three per-matrix formulas. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): all three twins fail, so this axis is RED. (1) mean_stable_rank/d_model (registered) repeats the geometry_spectral failure: stable rank is bit-identical (15.846333) when a fixed operator is zero-padded from d = 64 to 4096 while the twin falls 64x; it goes as d^+0.873 over 27 freshly analysed models and d^+0.668 over the 66-model archive, so dividing by d^1 over-corrects and flips the archive association from +0.637/+0.442 (d_model/n_layers) to -0.537 (p = 3e-06) / -0.502 (p = 2e-05). (2) mean_stable_rank_normalized = stable_rank/min(m,n) is the SAME divisor for a square projection -- it reproduces mean_stable_rank/d_model to all digits on all 14 multi-head models measured -- while on the 13 grouped-query models it inflates the value by a mean factor of 1.564 (sd 0.319, up to 2.166), because the K/V projections have min(m,n) = d_kv < d_model. It therefore replaces a width dependence with a dependence on the attention-head layout. (3) mean_rms_weight_scale = ||W||_F/sqrt(mn) is the only one with an exact mechanism (it is the RMS entry, an identity rather than a bound), but it does not remove the width term either: fan-in initialisation makes the RMS entry shrink with width, measured at d^-0.937 over the same 27 models, rho(d_model) = -0.594 (p = 0.002). None of the three is safe to hand a feature matrix.
fix_applied: R27: added dimensionless companions mean_stable_rank_normalized = stable_rank/min(m,n) (in [0,1] by construction; gpt2 0.05951, distilgpt2 0.05591) and mean_rms_weight_scale = ||W||_F/sqrt(mn) (gpt2 0.126844, distilgpt2 0.132348). The raw norms are architecture-conditioned -- mean_stable_rank has rho +0.683 with d_model over 61 models -- and these divide the shape term out using only the matrix's own dimensions, so they need no external divisor. The three per-matrix formulas are unchanged.
